blocks.text: Verses 18–23 shift from the public indictment of Judah to Jeremiah’s own endangered position. Readers often group passages like this with Jeremiah’s first-person laments or “confessions,” which can include accusation, isolation, protest, petition, and despair. The boundaries of that group and how directly it reflects Jeremiah’s biography remain disputed, but the passage plainly presents his appeal to God after learning that people from Anathoth seek to silence him.

Jeremiah belongs to a received book that combines poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration material, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix. A practical outline places chapters 2–25 within an extended opening collection, while recognizing that the book’s long compositional and textual history remains debated. This broader variety can help readers avoid expecting every chapter to work in the same literary mode.
